description.summary: shell commands to the compositor

protocol.description: Reserved to the Silica shell components (Dock, menu bar, Faro): the global is visible only to them. Windows are listed with ext-foreign-toplevel-list-v1; this protocol adds what the shell asks of the compositor.

request.name: activate

description.summary: brings a window to the front

request.description:
The window with this identifier (the identifier event of ext_foreign_toplevel_handle_v1) gets the focus and goes above the others, with its child windows above it; the other windows of its app stay where they are (a window picked in the Window menu, the Dock menu or Mission Control). If it is minimized, it comes back where it was; if its app is hidden, the app shows again. An unknown identifier does nothing.
Before version 10 this brought every window of the app forward, as activate_app does.

request.name: activate_app

description.summary: brings an app to the front

request.description: Activates the app of the window with this identifier, as a click on its Dock icon, the app switcher or Bring All to Front do: every window of the app on screen comes forward keeping their order, and this window goes on top with the focus. A minimized window comes back by itself; the app's other minimized windows stay minimized. An unknown identifier does nothing.

event.name: focused

description.summary: the focused window

event.description: The identifier (ext_foreign_toplevel_handle_v1.identifier) of the window that has the keyboard focus, or an empty string if no window has it. Sent on binding and on every change.

request.name: execute

description.summary: runs a catalog command

request.description: A parameterless command of the compositor's catalog (the same one used by shortcuts, the control channel and MCP), for example faro.toggle from the bar's magnifier.

event.name: command

description.summary: a command for the shell

event.description: A catalog command that belongs to a shell component (for example faro.toggle): The compositor forwards it to all of them; each one answers its own.

request.name: launch

description.summary: starts an app as a client of the session

request.description: The command (POSIX shell syntax, already without the Exec field codes) becomes a child process of the compositor, like app.launch on the control channel.

event.name: minimized

description.summary: a window was minimized or restored

event.description: The window with this identifier was minimized (minimized 1) or restored (0). On binding all minimized windows are sent, in the order they were minimized; then on every change. The Dock puts them next to the Trash.

request.name: thumbnail

description.summary: the thumbnail of a minimized window

request.description: the compositor writes into the file the window thumbnail (8-bit premultiplied RGBA, rows from the top, no padding between rows), taken when it was minimized, at most 256 pixels per side; then it sends the thumbnail event. The file must be writable and at least 256 × 256 × 4 bytes large.

event.name: thumbnail

description.summary: the thumbnail is in the file

event.description: Width and height of the thumbnail written into the file; 0 and 0 if the window is not minimized or has no thumbnail.

event.name: window_menu

description.summary: the arrangement popover of a window

event.description: Long press on the full-screen button of the window with this identifier: the shell opens the arrangement popover (move and resize, fill and arrange, full screen) with the tip towards the point x, y (logical screen coordinates, below the button). The entries run the window.tile_* commands on the focused window.

event.name: window_menu_appearance

description.summary: the appearance of the window of the next window_menu

event.description: Sent right before window_menu, for the same window: appearance is 0 when the window follows the system, 1 for light and 2 for dark (the window asked for it with silica_window_v1.set_appearance). The shell draws the popover in that appearance.

request.name: broadcast

description.summary: a state for the other shell components

request.description: A component announces a state to the others (for example the open Control Center, which the bar shows with the capsule on its icon): The compositor sends it back to every shell component with the broadcast event, sender included, and remembers it for whoever binds later.

event.name: broadcast

description.summary: the state announced by a component

event.description: On binding the last value of every topic, then on every announcement.

request.name: execute_with

description.summary: runs a catalog command with parameters

request.description: Like execute, with the parameters in JSON (an object): for example screenshot.region with the rectangle chosen in the crosshair.

enum.name: outside

description.summary: what an input outside an open transient does

enum.description: The version 6 rule, the same for every surface outside the transient: the pointer's hover always reaches the surfaces below. Since version 7 set_owned_transient replaces it with a rule for the owner app and one for the other surfaces.

entry.name: consume
entry.summary: it closes the transient and does nothing else

entry.name: pass_through
entry.summary: it closes the transient and also reaches what is below

request.name: set_transient

description.summary: a menu or panel of this surface is open

request.description: While a transient is open the surface keeps an input region as small as the menu or panel itself: the other windows keep receiving the pointer (hover, cursor shapes). A button press outside the transient makes the compositor send dismissed; then, per press, the press is consumed or delivered to what is under the pointer. Scrolling outside is delivered or dropped per scroll, without dismissing. A press on the surface itself (or its subsurfaces and popups) counts as inside, as does one inside region (surface coordinates; null: only the surface itself). Setting it again replaces the previous transient of the same surface. Keyboard routing stays with the layer surface's keyboard interactivity, which the shell sets while the transient is open.

request.name: clear_transient

description.summary: the transient of this surface is closed

request.description: The shell closed it itself (Esc, a choice, a toggle): no dismissed event follows.

enum.name: rule

description.summary: what the surfaces outside an open transient receive

enum.description: Whatever the rule, the wheel never ends a transient, and while one is open the compositor shows the arrow over every surface outside it (the text cursor is not shown: the window below does not have the keyboard).

entry.name: modal
entry.summary: no hover and no wheel; a press closes the transient and stops there

entry.name: pass
entry.summary: hover and wheel reach the surface; a press closes the transient and reaches it too

entry.name: activate
entry.summary: hover and wheel reach the surface; a primary press closes the transient and only activates the window under it, other buttons close it and reach the surface

request.name: set_owned_transient

description.summary: a menu or panel of this surface is open, with an owner app

request.description:
Like set_transient (the same surface, region, replacement, clear_transient and dismissed), with the outside split in two targets: the surfaces of the owner app follow owner_rule, every other surface follows other_rule. The owner is an app id (its windows, their popups and subsurfaces, and its desktop surface "desktop-icons:app-id"), "desktop-icons" for whichever app owns the desktop surface, "desktop-icons:app-id" for that app, or an empty string for the system (no owner app: every surface follows other_rule).
With a modal rule the pointer leaves the surfaces of that target while the transient is open (no hover, no tooltips) and wheel events there are dropped; a press there ends the transient and nothing else. An activate press ends the transient and gives the keyboard focus to the window under the pointer, raising it, without delivering the press or its drag: the window becomes active again and its content does not see the click.
When a press is outside several transients, the strictest outcome wins: modal, then activate, then pass.

event.name: dismissed

description.summary: a press outside closed the transient

event.description: The transient of this surface ended because of a press outside it; the shell closes the menu or panel. Sent once; the transient is already cleared.

event.name: app_menu

description.summary: the menus of the frontmost app

event.description: The menus the frontmost app published with silica-menu-v1, checked and rewritten by the compositor in the same JSON format, in a sealed file of size bytes from offset 0. app_id is the frontmost app (empty with none); serial names the app's menu object for activate_menu_item, 0 (with size 0) when the app published no menus. Sent on binding and every time the frontmost app or its menus change; while a menu or panel of the shell has the keyboard the frontmost app does not change.

request.name: activate_menu_item

description.summary: an item of the app's menus was chosen

request.description: the compositor sends activated with the id to the menu object with this serial, if it still exists; an old serial does nothing.

event.name: popup_menu

description.summary: an app asked for a context menu or a pop-up button's menu

event.description: The shell draws it (silica-os/silica-desktop#241). serial names the menu in the requests below. app_id is the owner app (its id for the transient's owner). The anchor is in output coordinates, logical pixels (a 0 × 0 rectangle for a context menu at the pointer, the control for a pop-up button); kind and selected are those of the app's request (0 context, 1 pop-up; selected 0 for none). The rows follow in popup_menu_row events and popup_menu_end closes the list; the shell opens the menu at the end. appearance is the app's window appearance as for window_menu_appearance.

event.name: popup_menu_row

description.summary: a row of the menu that is being sent

event.description: kind is a popup_row_kind. id, flags, icon, key and modifiers are those of the app's add_item (flags and icon also of begin_submenu); label also of add_section and begin_submenu; unused fields are empty or 0.

event.name: popup_menu_end

description.summary: the rows of the menu are complete

event.description: The shell may lay the menu out and show it.

event.name: popup_menu_closed

description.summary: the compositor ended the menu

event.description: A press outside, a change of context, the app or its surface going away: the shell fades the menu out. Sent once per menu, also after popup_menu_close and popup_menu_choose (then the menu is already closing on the shell's side).

request.name: popup_menu_transient

description.summary: where the open popup menu is

request.description: The shell's surface that draws the menu and the rectangles of the menu and its open submenu (surface coordinates, as set_owned_transient). The compositor already keeps the menu as a transient owned by the app (modal for the app, pass for everything else) from the moment the app showed it; this tells where it is, so that a press on it does not end it. Sent again whenever the rectangles change.

request.name: popup_menu_choose

description.summary: the user chose an item of the popup menu

request.description: the compositor sends selected(id) to the app and ends the menu. An old serial does nothing.

request.name: popup_menu_close

description.summary: the user closed the popup menu

request.description: Esc, or a click on nothing inside the shell's surface: the app is told dismissed.
